Safe Height Pty Ltd trading as SAFE MOUNT are a specialist provider of Height Safety Compliance  Solutions across SEQ. Our services include System Design, Installation of Height Safety Systems, Certification and Audit, as well as Harness & PPE Inspection services. Due to continued growth, we are seeking an experienced Project Administrator to support the planning, coordination and administration of multiple concurrent projects and service programs for the existing and new clients. The role requires regular travel along southeast Queensland between various projects with possible interstate trips. This role suits a highly capable, analytically-minded professional — potentially with an engineering, scientific, mining or other complex industrial background — who can quickly learn technical and regulatory frameworks, interpret data and adapt across multiple concurrent, complex projects as per various customers’ requirements. 

Skills
-  Project Coordination
-  Contract Administration
-  Contract Management

-  Microsoft Excel
-  Project Reporting
-  Contractor Management
-  Stakeholder Management

Main Duties / Responsibilities
-  Coordinate and administer height safety compliance inspection programs, system installation projects, and design services.
-  Develop, maintain and review project schedules, work programs, resource plans and project documentation.
-  Prepare and coordinate tender documentation, service agreements, work orders and contract documentation, ensuring project requirements, pricing, scope changes and approvals are accurately recorded throughout the project lifecycle.
-  Coordinate day-to-day communication and workflow between clients, engineers, contractors, installers, inspectors and suppliers to ensure activities are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project schedules.
-  Monitor project and service delivery performance against contractual requirements, compliance obligations and client expectations.
-  Act as a key point of contact for clients, contractors and suppliers by coordinating responses to project enquiries, facilitating communication between stakeholders and assisting with the timely resolution of operational issues.
-  Maintain accurate electronic project records, inspection reports, certification documentation, drawings, registers and compliance documentation to support project delivery and audit requirements.
-  Compile project performance information from multiple operational sources, analyse trends and prepare management reports covering project progress, productivity, compliance performance and service delivery outcomes.
-  Support project change management processes, including assessment, documentation and tracking of project variations.
-  Monitor contractor activities against agreed schedules, scopes of work and project milestones, identifying delays, quality concerns or scope changes requiring management review.
-  Support procurement and subcontractor coordination activities.
-  Prepare project documentation including client reports, operational summaries, project status updates, meeting papers and internal business documentation to support decision-making.
-  Provide project support to senior management by monitoring project risks, escalating critical issues, coordinating follow-up actions and assisting with implementation of operational decisions.
-  Identify delivery risks, compliance issues and operational constraints that may affect project schedules or client commitments.
-  Coordinate height safety inspection, installation and certification activities to ensure compliance with regulatory and client requirements.
-  Monitor contractor performance and support continuous improvement initiatives across projects and service programs.
Experience
-  To be considered for this role, applicants must demonstrate a minimum of 3 years’ experience in project coordination, project administration, project controls or similar project support roles within engineering, construction, industrial services, infrastructure, compliance or other relevant technical service environments. 

Performance Goals

-  Accurate and effective project reporting.
-  Efficient coordination of contractors, suppliers and stakeholders.

Other Requirements

How to Apply
Submit a resume and cover letter to info@safemount.com.au or via the application link.
We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds, regardless of age, gender, cultural background, disability or other protected attributes.

result.description: SDO  The Production Engineer is responsible for planning, developing and optimising manufacturing processes for the production of optical fibre current sensors, optical current transformers, transducers and related electrical monitoring equipment. The role focuses on improving manufacturing efficiency, product quality and production performance through engineering analysis, process optimisation and continuous improvement while ensuring compliance with engineering specifications, quality standards and workplace safety requirements.   Benefits   Task & responsibilities   Duties:    Plan and improve manufacturing processes for the production of optical fibre current sensors, current transformers, transducers and related electrical products.  Analyse production processes and identify opportunities to improve productivity, product quality and manufacturing efficiency.  Prepare and maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and process specifications.  Coordinate production activities to ensure products are manufactured on time and meet quality standards.  Investigate production issues, equipment faults and product defects, and implement corrective actions.  Monitor production performance and recommend process improvements to enhance efficiency and reduce waste.  Support the introduction of new products through production trials, process validation and manufacturing implementation.  Evaluate manufacturing equipment and recommend upgrades or process improvements to improve production performance.  Ensure manufacturing activities comply with engineering specifications, quality standards, workplace health and safety requirements and relevant Australian standards.  Work closely with Engineering, Quality, Production and Supply Chain teams to support continuous improvement and achieve production objectives.    Responsibilities:    Ensure manufacturing processes operate efficiently and achieve production and quality targets.  Maintain accurate engineering and production documentation.  Provide technical support to production staff and assist in resolving manufacturing issues.  Monitor product quality and ensure compliance with engineering specifications and company standards.  Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and implement practical engineering solutions.  Support equipment commissioning, process validation and engineering change implementation.  Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) policies and company procedures.  Collaborate with internal teams to support production planning and timely customer delivery.     Qualification & experience   Bachelor's degree or higher in Production Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.  Minimum of one (1) year of relevant full-time work experience as a Production Engineer or in a similar manufacturing engineering role.  Knowledge of manufacturing processes, production planning and process improvement.  Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.  Understanding of quality management systems and workplace health and safety (WHS) requirements.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  Good communication and teamwork skills.  Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with ERP/MRP systems or manufacturing software is an advantage.   About Company    Founded in Sydney in 2004, Smart Digital Optics (SDO) manufactures optical fibre current sensors for the electric power and smelting industries. Smart Digital Optics is one of the first companies to incorporate optical fibre current sensors into power monitoring and metering systems allowing users to measure electric currents with unprecedented levels of accuracy and ease. The digitally compatible and compact SDO products offer superior utility and performance compared to costly and cumbersome traditional approaches.  In 2010 SDO formed a strategic alliance with the Arteche Group. Arteche has 65 years of experience in the manufacture of electrical power products for generation, transmission, distribution and industrial applications. As an international benchmark with equipment in service in over 150 countries, it has companies in Europe, America, Asia and Oceania, as well as a service network comprised of more than 80 technical and sales offices.  The combination of SDO’s technology expertise with Arteche’s long experience in the electricity sector provides customers with a partner well equipped to support the introduce new technology for advanced transmission and industrial systems.   Technology :   SDO uses its expertise in advanced optics and signal processing to develop solutions for power engineering applications.  SDO’s optical current sensors utilize the Faraday effect in optical fibre, whereby the state of polarization of the light propagating in the fibre interacts with the magnetic field around a conductor.This effect is highly linear and provides the basis of an ultra high bandwidth, wide dynamic range current sensor which measures both AC and DC current with high accuracy. result.description:
The Client 

Blaze Engineering and Sheetmetal Fabrication Pty Ltd is a metal fabrication and engineering business based in Tullamarine, VIC, specialising in sheet metal fabrication, welding, metal assembly, and engineered manufacturing solutions.  

They are seeking an experienced Welder (First Class) to join their team in Tullamarine, VIC. 

 

The Role 

The Welder (First Class) is responsible for fabricating, assembling, and repairing metal components and structures using a range of welding and fabrication techniques. 

This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $78,000 to $82,000 plus superannuation. 

 

The Responsibilities 

Select and prepare appropriate welding equipment, consumables, and materials for welding operations. 

Read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, welding procedures, and specifications to determine welding requirements. 

Mark out and cut metal sections and components using metal-cutting machinery. 

Shape and bend metal sections and plates using machine tools. 

Set up and operate MIG welding equipment to weld, join, and repair metal components and structures. 

Position and secure workpieces to ensure accurate alignment and welding in accordance with specifications. 

Perform welding operations on various metal components while maintaining required quality and safety standards. 

Inspect completed welds to ensure compliance with specified dimensions, quality requirements, and welding standards. 

Repair defective welds and damaged metal components through grinding, gouging, and rewelding processes. 

Perform weld finishing activities, including grinding and dressing welds to achieve the required finish and appearance. 

Use measuring and testing instruments to verify weld quality, accuracy, and compliance with specifications. 

Carry out welding repairs and maintenance on metal structures, machinery, equipment, and related components. 

Clean and prepare metal surfaces before and after welding to ensure quality. 

Conduct routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting of welding equipment to ensure safe and efficient operation. 

Follow workplace health and safety procedures, welding safety requirements, and relevant industry regulations at all times. 

Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, inspectors, and other trades personnel to complete welding tasks efficiently. 

Maintain accurate records of welding activities, inspections, repairs, materials used, and work completed. 

 

The Requirements 

Certificate IV in Engineering or equivalent qualification 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience as a Welder (First Class) or within metal fabrication environments 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience performing MIG welding across structural steel and fabricated metal components 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience interpreting engineering drawings, fabrication plans, and technical specifications 

At least 1.5 years’ experience operating fabrication machinery, welding equipment, and metalworking tools 

At least 1.5 years’ experience assembling, repairing, and finishing fabricated metal products to engineering standards 

Sound knowledge of a range of welding techniques, including TIG, flux-cored and manual metal arc welding, and their application in metal fabrication. 

Strong knowledge of welding procedures, fabrication methods, and metal finishing techniques 

Ability to identify welding defects, dimensional inconsistencies, and fabrication issues accurately 

Strong understanding of workplace safety procedures, fabrication compliance standards, and workshop operations 

Good communication skills and ability to work effectively within fabrication and engineering teams 

High attention to detail and commitment to precision workmanship
